title: Source-isomorphism and signed-shift transport of the internal-Hom colimit comparison
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small in the chosen universe, with $\mathcal O$ commutative [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention]. Put $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ and use its ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal M)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Fix the functorial K-injective target models for $H(A,N)=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(A,N)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, def-sfb-internal-hom-strict-models]. For any small filtered diagram $N:I\to\operatorname{CoCh}(\mathcal M)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], put $N_\infty=\varinjlim_iN_i$ termwise and let $\alpha_A:\varinjlim_iH(A,N_i)\to H(A,N_\infty)$ be the image in $D(\mathcal M)$ of the canonical complex cocone map on these models. All colimits here are termwise sheaf colimits. The comparison is independent, up to the canonical identifications, of the complex representative of $A$. For every source isomorphism $e:A\xrightarrow{\sim}A'$ the precomposition isomorphisms satisfy
$$H(e,N_\infty)\circ\alpha_{A'}=\alpha_A\circ\varinjlim_i H(e,N_i).$$
For every $n\in\mathbf Z$, let $s_{A,n,N}:H(A[n],N)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(A,N)[-n]$ be the signed source-shift comparison, with cochain convention $K[n]^q=K^{q+n}$ and $d_{K[n]}=(-1)^n d_K$: on the Hom-complex models, for a complex $\mathcal L$ representing $A$ and the fixed K-injective model $\mathcal I$ of $N$, it is the chain isomorphism which reindexes $\prod_p\mathcal Hom(\mathcal L^{p+n},\mathcal I^{p+q})=\prod_{p'}\mathcal Hom(\mathcal L^{p'},\mathcal I^{p'+q-n})$ and multiplies degree-$q$ components by $(-1)^{nq}$; its sign depends only on $n,q$, not on $N$ (any normalization differing from it by a sign depending only on $n$ gives the same assertions). Let
$$t:\varinjlim_iH(A[n],N_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}(\varinjlim_iH(A,N_i))[-n]$$
be induced by the $s_{A,n,N_i}$ and the termwise colimit-shift identification. Then
$$s_{A,n,N_\infty}\circ\alpha_{A[n]}=\alpha_A[-n]\circ t.$$
These squares are natural in the target diagram. In particular their horizontal maps are conjugate by isomorphisms. No continuity or boundedness hypothesis is imposed on $A$ or $N$.

proof.text:
Write $J$ for the fixed functorial K-injective replacement and put $B_L(T)=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(L,J(T))$ for a source complex $L$. These are exactly the strict models in the statement, by [def-sfb-internal-hom-strict-models, def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For the colimit cocone $u_i:N_i\to N_\infty$, set $C_L=\operatorname{colim}_i B_L(N_i)$ and let $a_L:C_L\to B_L(N_\infty)$ be the unique map with $a_L\iota_i=B_L(u_i)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The termwise construction is a colimit of complexes: the induced differential squares to zero and the degreewise universal maps commute with it, as can be checked after each colimit injection. For a chain map $v:L\to L'$, precomposition and postcomposition commute componentwise [def-pur-hom-complex], so
$$B_v(N_\infty)B_{L'}(u_i)=B_L(u_i)B_v(N_i).$$
Precomposing with each $\iota_i$ proves $B_v(N_\infty)a_{L'}=a_L\operatorname{colim}_i B_v(N_i)$ as an equality of chain maps. Thus $L\mapsto a_L$ is a contravariant functor to the category of arrows of complexes.

proof.text: The category $\mathcal M$ has all small colimits and exact filtered colimits by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian]; its small-site and commutative-coefficient hypotheses are precisely those assumed here. Apply [src-weil-homology-preserves-exact-colimits] with $\mathcal C=\mathcal M$, the given small filtered category $I$, and the cochain shape on $\mathbf Z$. For every integer $q$, this gives the natural identification $H^q(\operatorname{colim}_i X_i)=\operatorname{colim}_i H^q(X_i)$. Consequently a natural transformation of $I$-diagrams of complexes which is a quasi-isomorphism at every index induces a quasi-isomorphism of termwise colimits: after this identification its $q$-th cohomology map is the colimit of an objectwise isomorphism, whose inverse is the colimit of the inverse natural transformation. There is no boundedness condition in the cited homology statement.

proof.text: If $v:L\to L'$ is a quasi-isomorphism, apply [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined] with source map $v$ and target map $1_{J(T)}$. It says that $B_v(T):B_{L'}(T)\to B_L(T)$ is a quasi-isomorphism for every $T$; both target complexes are the same K-injective complex. These maps form a natural transformation in $T$ by step 1. Step 2 shows that $\operatorname{colim}_i B_v(N_i)$ is also a quasi-isomorphism. Let $Q$ be the derived localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The arrow-valued functor $L\mapsto Q(a_L)$ therefore sends every source quasi-isomorphism to an isomorphism of arrows: both its endpoint maps are isomorphisms, and their inverses give an inverse square. By the universal property of localization it factors through $D(\mathcal M)^{\mathrm{op}}$. Its right endpoint is $A\mapsto H(A,N_\infty)$ by [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], and its left endpoint is the meaning of the termwise-colimit model with variable derived source. Its arrow at $A$ is $\alpha_A$. This constructs the canonical representative identifications and proves independence of the source representative; the identifications depend only on its specified identification with $A$, by uniqueness of the factorization.

proof.text:
For $e:A\xrightarrow{\sim}A'$, apply the functor of arrows constructed in step 3 to $e$ (contravariantly). Its right endpoint is $H(e,N_\infty)$ and its left endpoint is the induced map denoted $\operatorname{colim}_i H(e,N_i)$. The fact that it is a morphism of arrows is exactly
$$H(e,N_\infty)\alpha_{A'}=\alpha_A\operatorname{colim}_iH(e,N_i).$$
Applying the same functor to $e^{-1}$ gives inverses to both vertical maps. In particular this notation for a derived source isomorphism does not require a chain-map representative of $e$: the maps are defined by the localized construction of step 3. For a chain-map representative they recover step 1.

proof.text: The general existence of a source-shift natural isomorphism of sheaf Hom complexes is [lem-pur-hom-complex-shift-left]. To specify the normalization used here, use the product and differential in [def-pur-hom-complex]: in degree $q$ reindex $p'=p+n$ and multiply by $c_q=(-1)^{nq}$. The inverse reindexes back and multiplies by the same $c_q$, whose square is $1$. After reindexing, the domain differential on $f$ is $d_Jf-(-1)^{q+n}fd_L$, while the differential on $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(L,J(T))[-n]$ is $(-1)^nd_Jf-(-1)^qfd_L$. Since $c_{q+1}=(-1)^nc_q$, multiplying these two expressions gives exactly $s^{q+1}d=d s^q$. Thus the stated map is a chain isomorphism. Postcomposition with $J(h)$ for any chain map $h:T\to T'$ commutes with this reindexing and scalar. It is therefore natural in $T$, with a sign independent of $T$, and its image under $Q$ is the specified $s_{A,n,T}$.

proof.text:
For any diagram $X_i$ of complexes, the termwise-colimit shift identification $\operatorname{colim}_i(X_i[-n])\cong(\operatorname{colim}_i X_i)[-n]$ is the identity under $(\operatorname{colim}_i X_i[-n])^q=\operatorname{colim}_i X_i^{q-n}$. The differentials agree because both are $(-1)^n$ times the differential induced from the $X_i$, and the structure maps agree in each degree. Apply this to $X_i=B_L(N_i)$ and take the colimit of the chain isomorphisms of step 5. Their inverses likewise induce an inverse, giving the chain-level map whose image is $t$. Naturality of step 5 for $u_i$ says
$$s_{L,n,N_\infty}B_{L[n]}(u_i)=B_L(u_i)[-n]s_{L,n,N_i}.$$
Compose the two candidate maps from $\operatorname{colim}_iB_{L[n]}(N_i)$ with each colimit injection. They are equal by this formula and by the defining equations for $a_L$ and $a_{L[n]}$. Uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives equality of the chain maps. Applying $Q$, which commutes with shifts by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], proves $s_{A,n,N_\infty}\alpha_{A[n]}=\alpha_A[-n]t$.

proof.text: For a natural transformation $h:N\to N'$ of target diagrams, its colimit $h_\infty$ satisfies $h_\infty u_i=u'_i h_i$. Functoriality of $J$ and postcomposition give $B_L(h_\infty)a_L=a'_L\operatorname{colim}_iB_L(h_i)$ after testing on each injection, exactly as in step 1. Precomposition by a source map commutes with these postcompositions; step 3 retains these equalities under localization. The source-shift maps commute with them by the degreewise formula of step 5, as does the colimit-shift identification of step 6. This proves naturality of both squares in the target diagram. Solving the squares gives $\alpha_A=H(e,N_\infty)\alpha_{A'}(\operatorname{colim}_iH(e,N_i))^{-1}$ and $\alpha_{A[n]}=s_{A,n,N_\infty}^{-1}\alpha_A[-n]t$, the asserted conjugations. Every argument used arbitrary integer degrees and arbitrary complexes; filteredness was used only for step 2.
